sources.title: Answer Batch 0029 House Robber source-first relation review

claims.text: The two consolidated source Questions represent the same linear House Robber / LeetCode 198 problem with non-adjacent selection and an explicit non-negative amount array in the more detailed wording.
For each position every legal optimum either skips the current house or takes it and excludes the previous house, yielding max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).
The executable fixture verifies empty/singleton behavior, standard recurrence examples, the local-greedy counterexample, all-zero values and the example null contract.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS empty=0 single=5 canonical-example=4 second-example=12 greedy-counterexample=4 zeros=0 null=rejected

findings: Both current source Questions are covered: the generic House Robber/simple-DP wording and the explicit LeetCode 198 non-negative-array/non-adjacent contract resolve to one Canonical and one answer boundary.

The candidate contains a complete compilable Java class, states the exhaustive recurrence max(skip current, take current plus i-2), explains the optimal-substructure argument and rolling-state invariant, and gives O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary space.

The candidate explicitly separates source facts from example-interface choices: empty-array behavior, null rejection, Java language choice and long accumulation are not presented as preserved source requirements.
The deterministic Java fixture passes empty, singleton, standard examples, all-zero input, a [2,1,1,2] counterexample to local greedy reasoning, and explicit null rejection.
The answer excludes the circular House Robber II contract and does not fabricate project experience, production scale, version facts or unsupported source constraints.
No uncovered source variant, unsupported source claim, coding hard failure or correctness blocker remains. Formal promotion remains subject to the repository promotion/real-review policy.
